text:
Braden Schneider has become a talking point in New York for the wrong reasons. Blue Seat Blogs called him "a mystery for the New York Rangers," and BVM Sports asked whether it is time to move on. Through 20 games the 2020 first-rounder has two assists, no goals and 30 shots, at 0.32 points per 60 minutes.

Here's the twist: the Rangers keep leaning on him. His ice time has climbed to 19.7 minutes over his last ten games, up more than two minutes from before, and he played 23.4 in the win at Calgary. And his on-ice 5v5 results are decent: 52.7% of expected goals, roughly level with his team. His physical game (46 hits, 25 blocks) and skating are intact, with top speed and burst counts in the upper quarter of the league.

The points were never his calling card. Evolving-Hockey had him in the bottom 1% of defensemen for offense created last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flagged his exits (30% with possession). Our range has him around 15 points for the season. The real question is whether he can move the puck cleanly enough to justify the minutes.
headline: Schneider's scoring has gone quiet, his minutes haven't
